record.summary: Two companion guides from the Japan AI Safety Institute for AI developers and AI providers. The Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety sets out concepts for evaluating the AI safety of LLM systems and AI agent systems: perspectives such as control of toxic output, fairness and inclusion, privacy protection, ensuring security, robustness and verifiability, with example risks and evaluation items, evaluators, timing and methods; version 1.20 adds 'observation and control' for AI agent systems. The Guide to Red Teaming Methodology on AI Safety covers evaluating the risk countermeasures of LLM systems from an attacker's perspective, from attack methods and roles to a 15-step process.

verification.note: Stored on 11 Oct 2026: J-AISI's release page for the Evaluation Perspectives Guide v1.20 (7 Jul 2026), the full Japanese text of v1.20 and its Japanese summary slides, and the release page for the Red Teaming Methodology Guide v1.10. Stored on 14 Oct 2026: J-AISI's outputs list (Information), the Japanese text of the Red Teaming Methodology Guide v1.10 (31 Mar 2025), and J-AISI's English versions of the Evaluation Perspectives Guide v1.10 and the Red Teaming Methodology Guide v1.10, each marked 'Please refer to the original text for accuracy'. The outputs list confirms every version date in notes, including first publication on 18 Sept 2024 (evaluation guide) and 25 Sept 2024 (red-teaming guide), and the healthcare and AI robotics guides. No English version of v1.20 is linked from its release page; english_version points at the English v1.10 of the evaluation guide. The summary is written from the Japanese texts, with the evaluation perspectives named as J-AISI's English renders them.
